title: AWL Sublist 6
description: Las 60 palabras de la sublista 6 de la Academic Word List, con definición, traducción, ejemplo académico, colocaciones y familia léxica.

cards.definition: Based on general ideas rather than real, concrete things; also, a short summary of a research paper.
cards.example: Young children often struggle with abstract concepts such as justice or probability.
cards.warning: En un artículo científico, "abstract" es el resumen inicial, no algo "abstracto".

cards.definition: Correct and exact in every detail.
cards.example: Accurate data on rural employment are difficult to obtain in developing countries.
cards.warning: 'Accurate' = correcto, sin errores (datos, cifras, descripciones); no significa 'acertado' en el sentido de 'oportuno' (eso es 'appropriate' o 'wise').

cards.definition: To accept or admit that something is true or exists; to recognise someone's contribution.
cards.example: The authors acknowledge that their sample was too small to support firm conclusions.

cards.definition: A total formed by combining several separate amounts or items.
cards.example: Aggregate demand fell sharply during the first two quarters of the recession.

cards.definition: To officially give something, such as money or time, for a particular purpose.
cards.example: The government allocated a larger share of the budget to primary healthcare.

cards.definition: To give someone a job or task; to decide that something has a particular value or role.
cards.example: Participants were randomly assigned to either the control group or the experimental group.

cards.definition: To fasten or join one thing to another; to consider something as having importance.
cards.example: Many voters attach great importance to a candidate's economic record.

cards.definition: The writer of a book, article or report; to write such a text.
cards.example: The author argues that urban sprawl increases dependence on private cars.
cards.warning: No confundir con "authority" (autoridad) ni "authorise" (autorizar).

cards.definition: A close connection between people or things; also a certificate of debt issued by a government or company.
cards.example: Shared hardship can strengthen the social bonds within a community.

cards.definition: Lasting only a short time or using few words; to give someone essential information.
cards.example: This essay will give a brief overview of the main causes of deforestation.

cards.definition: Having the ability or skill needed to do something.
cards.example: Few existing batteries are capable of storing energy for long periods.
cards.warning: Se dice "capable OF doing", nunca "capable to do".

cards.definition: To mention something as an example or proof; to quote or refer to a source.
cards.example: Critics often cite rising inequality as evidence that the policy has failed.
cards.warning: No confundir con "site" (sitio) ni "sight" (vista): suenan igual. Tampoco significa "citar" en el sentido de quedar con alguien (eso es "arrange to meet").

cards.definition: To work together with others to achieve a shared goal.
cards.example: Neighbouring countries must cooperate to manage shared water resources.

cards.definition: To treat a person or group unfairly; also, to recognise a difference between things.
cards.example: It is illegal for employers to discriminate against applicants on the basis of age.
cards.warning: Lleva preposición: "discriminate AGAINST someone".

cards.definition: To show something so people can see it; to show a feeling or quality.
cards.example: The results are displayed in Table 2, broken down by age group.

cards.definition: Very different from each other; including many different types of people or things.
cards.example: Large cities tend to have more culturally diverse populations than rural areas.
cards.warning: "Diverse" significa "variado", no "varios": para "diversos estudios" es mejor "several/various studies".

cards.definition: An area of knowledge, activity or responsibility.
cards.example: Privacy has become a central issue in the domain of public health.
cards.warning: No significa "dominio" en el sentido de "dominar un idioma" (eso es "command/mastery").

cards.definition: To prepare a text by correcting and improving it; to be responsible for a book or journal.
cards.example: The volume was edited by three researchers from different universities.
cards.warning: "Edit" no es "publicar" ("publish"). Una "edición" es "edition"; la "editorial" (empresa) es "publisher".

cards.definition: To improve the quality, value or strength of something.
cards.example: Regular feedback can significantly enhance students' writing skills.

cards.definition: A large area of land with one owner; all the property a person owns, especially at death.
cards.example: Rising real estate prices have pushed many young families out of the city centre.
cards.warning: No es "estado" ("state"). "Real estate" = bienes inmuebles.

cards.definition: To be greater than a particular number or amount; to go beyond a limit.
cards.example: In 2022, demand for electricity exceeded supply for the first time.
cards.warning: Verbo transitivo: "exceed 50%", no "exceed TO 50%".

cards.definition: A person with special knowledge or skill in a particular area.
cards.example: Most experts agree that the shift to renewable energy is now unavoidable.

cards.definition: Stated clearly and directly, so that there is no doubt about the meaning.
cards.example: The guidelines make explicit reference to the rights of disabled workers.

cards.definition: Relating to a central government that shares power with regional states or provinces.
cards.example: Federal funding for scientific research rose steadily during the 1960s.

cards.definition: An amount of money paid for a service or for the right to do something.
cards.example: Raising tuition fees may discourage students from low-income families.

cards.definition: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.
cards.example: Flexible working hours can help parents balance work and childcare.

cards.definition: Used to add another point that supports what has already been said.
cards.example: Public transport reduces congestion. Furthermore, it lowers carbon emissions per passenger.
cards.warning: Va al principio de la frase seguido de coma. No lo repitas: alterna con "Moreover", "In addition".

cards.definition: The state of being male or female, especially in social and cultural terms.
cards.example: The study found a significant gender gap in access to higher education.
cards.warning: No sirve para "género" literario o musical (eso es "genre") ni para "mercancía" ("goods").

cards.definition: Lack of knowledge or information about something.
cards.example: Public ignorance of the environmental cost of fast fashion remains widespread.
cards.warning: "Ignore" NO significa "ignorar = no saber", sino "no hacer caso". "Ignorar" algo (no saberlo) = "be unaware of" o "not know".

cards.definition: Something that encourages a person to do something, often money or a reward.
cards.example: Tax incentives could persuade companies to invest in cleaner technology.

cards.definition: How often something, especially something bad like a disease, happens.
cards.example: The incidence of type 2 diabetes has risen in almost every country.
cards.warning: No confundir con "incident" (suceso, incidente concreto).

cards.definition: To include something as part of a larger whole.
cards.example: The new curriculum incorporates environmental education into science lessons.
cards.warning: No significa "incorporarse" a un trabajo (eso es "join" o "start").

cards.definition: A number or system that shows the level of something; an alphabetical list at the end of a book.
cards.example: The consumer price index rose by 3% over the twelve-month period.
cards.warning: El "índice" de un libro al principio es "contents"; "index" es el índice alfabético del final.

cards.definition: To slow down, limit or prevent a process or activity.
cards.example: High interest rates may inhibit investment by small businesses.

cards.definition: To make something begin, especially a plan, process or action.
cards.example: The city council initiated a programme to plant ten thousand trees.

cards.definition: Ideas, information, money or effort put into a process to make it work.
cards.example: Local residents should have input into decisions about new housing developments.

cards.definition: To tell someone to do something officially; to teach someone a skill.
cards.example: Participants were instructed to record their food intake every evening.

cards.definition: The ability to learn, understand and think; also, secret information about enemies.
cards.example: Artificial intelligence is transforming the way medical images are analysed.

cards.definition: A period of time between two events, or a space between two points.
cards.example: Blood pressure was measured at regular intervals throughout the day.

cards.definition: A formal talk given to students or an audience on a particular subject.
cards.example: Recorded lectures allow students to review difficult material at their own pace.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "lecture" NO es "lectura" (eso es "reading").

cards.definition: To move from one place or country to another, especially to live or work.
cards.example: Millions of workers migrated from rural areas to coastal cities in search of jobs.

cards.definition: The smallest amount or level that is possible or allowed.
cards.example: Raising the minimum wage could lift many workers out of poverty.

cards.definition: A government department led by a minister.
cards.example: The Ministry of Education plans to introduce coding lessons in all primary schools.

cards.definition: A reason for doing something, especially one that is hidden.
cards.example: Profit is not the only motive behind corporate charity programmes.
cards.warning: Para "motivo" en general ("por este motivo") se usa más "reason": "for this reason".

cards.definition: Not supporting either side in an argument or conflict; having no strong qualities.
cards.example: Researchers should use neutral language when writing survey questions.

cards.definition: Despite what has just been said; however.
cards.example: The experiment had several flaws. Nevertheless, its findings were later confirmed.
cards.warning: Introduce un contraste tras una idea ya dicha; no se usa como "although" para unir dos cláusulas.

cards.definition: In, to or from foreign countries, especially those across the sea.
cards.es: extranjero, en el extranjero, de ultramar
cards.example: The number of overseas students in Australia doubled within a decade.
cards.warning: Como adverbio no lleva preposición: "study overseas", no "study in overseas".

cards.definition: To happen or exist before something else.
cards.example: The financial crisis was preceded by a long period of easy credit.
cards.warning: No confundir con "proceed" (continuar, proceder).

cards.definition: To think something is true without being certain or having proof.
cards.example: It is often presumed that older workers are less adaptable, but evidence suggests otherwise.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "presume" NO es "presumir" ("show off" / "boast").

cards.definition: Based on clear thinking and reason rather than emotion.
cards.example: Classical economics assumes that consumers make rational choices.

cards.definition: To return to a normal state after an illness or difficulty; to get something back.
cards.example: Tourism took almost three years to recover after the pandemic.

cards.definition: To make known something that was secret or previously unknown.
cards.example: The survey revealed that most commuters would switch to rail if it were cheaper.

cards.definition: The range of things that a subject, study or activity deals with; opportunity to do something.
cards.example: A detailed cost analysis is beyond the scope of this essay.

cards.definition: Money that a government pays to reduce the cost of a product or service.
cards.example: Farm subsidies keep food prices low but may harm producers in poorer countries.

cards.definition: A narrow strip of material used for sticking or recording; to record sound or video.
cards.example: Interviews were taped and later transcribed for analysis.
cards.warning: "Red tape" = burocracia (no "cinta roja").

cards.definition: To find the origin or development of something; a very small amount or sign of something.
cards.example: The tradition can be traced back to the early medieval period.

cards.definition: To change something completely, usually improving it.
cards.example: Mobile banking has transformed financial services in parts of East Africa.

cards.definition: A system for carrying people or goods; to move them from one place to another.
cards.example: Investment in public transport is essential to reduce urban air pollution.
cards.warning: En inglés británico "public transport"; en americano "public transportation".

cards.definition: To be the real cause or basis of something, often not obvious.
cards.example: Poverty and poor housing often underlie health inequalities.
cards.warning: La forma más útil es el adjetivo "underlying": "the underlying cause".

cards.definition: To use something, especially in an effective or practical way.
cards.example: Many hospitals fail to utilise the data they already collect.
cards.warning: No abuses de "utilise" en lugar de "use": suena pomposo. Úsalo para "aprovechar" recursos.
